subsystems.name: Core and support structure
subsystems.role: supplies the anchor and, for the innermost layer, most of the gravity; everything else is built around it.
parts: load-bearing lattice of struts and rings

subsystems.name: Shell decks
subsystems.role: the nested concentric surfaces that carry soil, water, buildings and people.

subsystems.name: Atmosphere and biosphere
subsystems.role: holds a breathable gas mix at the right pressure and keeps an ecosystem alive on an artificial surface.

subsystems.name: Illumination system
subsystems.role: delivers light to surfaces that see no natural sky.
parts: skylights or windows in the deck above

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: radiates the waste heat that every biosphere and every machine produces.

subsystems.name: Access and transport
subsystems.role: moves people and cargo between layers and to the outside.

buildSteps.title: Choose the central body
buildSteps.detail: Select a small moon or asteroid of the right mass and composition, and survey it for metals, silicates and volatiles. Its mass is fixed first, because it sets the gravity felt on the innermost layer.

buildSteps.title: Build the material supply chain
buildSteps.detail: Set up mass drivers and solar furnaces on the body itself, streaming refined structural material into orbit. The tonnage is planetary, so mining, refining and assembly would have to be largely automated and self-replicating.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the support skeleton
buildSteps.detail: Fly in a lattice of struts and rings in sections and join them in orbit around the core. Where static strength alone cannot carry the span, powered active-support elements continuously move ballast masses to hold the structure up.

buildSteps.title: Lay the first deck
buildSteps.detail: Cover the skeleton with plates of structural material to make a continuous surface, leaving expansion joints and corridors for cables, coolant and traffic.

buildSteps.title: Establish gravity
buildSteps.detail: Rotate the shell so its surface experiences the intended acceleration; the rim speed must stay within what the material can bear. A layer built close in around a massive core can instead rely on the core's own gravity.

buildSteps.title: Seal in an atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Pressure-seal the deck, raise rim walls or a whole outer skin, then add gas, water and soil at the right pressure and composition.

buildSteps.title: Light and cool it
buildSteps.detail: A lattice of orbiting mirrors steers sunlight in through skylights. The same shell must also radiate the waste heat the ecosystem generates, or the interior will cook itself.

buildSteps.title: Seed and commission
buildSteps.detail: Introduce microbes, plants and later animal communities, then monitor pressure, temperature and gas balance over decades until the closed cycles hold steady.

buildSteps.title: Repeat outward
buildSteps.detail: Each further shell is built on the same pattern at a larger radius, with its own illumination, atmosphere and ecosystem, until the nested stack is complete.

prerequisites.why: a shellworld consumes more material than a planet's worth of industry could deliver from Earth.
spacecraft and stations are assembled in orbit today, but not at the scale or precision a shell requires.

prerequisites.tech: Closed-loop life support at ecosystem scale
prerequisites.why: sealed habitat experiments have run for months to a few years, not for the generations a shellworld biosphere needs.
holding up a shell thousands of kilometres across needs powered support that has never been built at any scale.

prerequisites.tech: Materials strong enough for high rim speeds
prerequisites.why: rotating a shell fast enough to give Earth-like gravity demands specific strength beyond today's bulk engineering materials.

prerequisites.tech: Space-based power at very large scale
prerequisites.why: illumination, pumping and cooling all need continuous power gathered outside the shell.

pathway.milestone: orbital stations and sealed habitats practising long-duration life support
pathway.unlocks: knowledge of how closed loops fail over time.

pathway.milestone: rotating habitat demonstrators tens of metres across, plus early asteroid prospecting
mass drivers and orbital rings moving bulk material cheaply, with gigawatt-scale solar collection
pathway.unlocks: the ability to shift planetary masses of rock and metal.

pathway.milestone: a single free-flying shell with its own atmosphere and ecosystem, built around a small body
pathway.unlocks: a biosphere that does not depend on a planet at all.
habitable area many times that of a planet, without needing a second star.
